shouldFix.title: The new fourth retained item is labelled memberVerbatim but carries no member of the live three-member evidence cell, NT-7's supplies list gives a third differently-worded rendering, and nothing records that retainedEvidence now holds four entries against a three-member cell
shouldFix.location: retainedEvidence[3].memberVerbatim, namedCorpusClasses NT-7 suppliesMembers, and the absence of any live-cell member statement
shouldFix.finding: The live evidence cell splits on semicolon into exactly three members, and the subject quotes that cell correctly at liveCellVerbatim. retainedEvidence now holds four entries. The first three carry memberVerbatim strings equal to the three live members. The fourth carries 'host must not mint fail/warn other than core policyOutcome', which is not among them. I checked what it is instead: it is the live claim cell's first limb with the leading capital dropped — the register reads 'Host must not mint fail/warn other than core policyOutcome', and case-insensitively the two are identical, so this is a near-verbatim claim quote, not an invented phrase. But it sits in a field named memberVerbatim, and it is verbatim from nothing: not from the evidence cell, whose members that field names everywhere else in this artifact and across its siblings, and not quite from the claim either. NT-7's corpus object compounds it. Its suppliesMembers reads 'host-minted fail/warn other than core policyOutcome' — a third wording, not equal to the fourth entry's string and not a substring of the claim in any casing, so it quotes nothing at all. Against that, NT-8's suppliesMembers lists the three live members exactly, which is the standard the NT-7 side does not meet. And nothing in the artifact says the live cell has three members while four are retained: there is no liveCellMemberSplit and no note anywhere.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: Every sibling specification in this corpus keys retainedEvidence to the live evidence cell and carries a block enumerating those members and refusing invented extras by name. A reader or a recording act comparing this artifact to the DR-G28 row sees four members against a three-member cell with no explanation. The harm is bounded — liveCellVerbatim is right there in the same file, so the live cell is recoverable from the artifact itself — which is why this is a SHOULD-FIX and not a blocker.
shouldFix.whatIAmNotSaying: I am not faulting the decision to add a fourth item. My v1 repair note offered exactly that — 'either as a fourth retained item bound to the claim's first limb, or as a named limb of EV-2 with its own retained bytes' — and the candidate took the first option, which closes the coverage hole cleanly. What I did not offer, and would not have, is labelling it memberVerbatim. That part is mine to have specified and I did not, so I record the omission as a labelling defect rather than a failure to follow the repair.
shouldFix.whatWouldRepairIt: Quote the claim's first limb exactly, capital H included, and put it under a field that says what it is — claimLimbVerbatim, or memberVerbatim omitted with a suppliesClaimLimb marker — so the field name stops asserting membership. Make NT-7's suppliesMembers use that same string rather than a third wording. Add one sentence, or a liveCellMemberSplit block in the sibling idiom, recording that the live evidence cell has three members, that all three are supplied by NT-8, and that the fourth retained item exists because the live cell's members do not reach the claim's first limb, which is NT-7's.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX. Thirteen attacks run, one landed. Custody holds: subject 1a2747a5 at 0444, 9756 bytes, unmoved and unedited; frozen v1 at ad5a17b3 and my v1 verdict at d62eb4ec both agreeing with the dispatch and stable; HEAD never left 5d5d778; file 08 equal to the subject's own pin; required-now 26 of 26. Six of six cited digests reproduce. All three findings landed in substance, and two of them landed completely. B1's coverage hole is closed: NT-7's evidence is now retained twice, in EV-4 and in the NT-7 corpus-class object, and EV-4's intent carries the CoreCompletion anchor that NT-7's input names and that occurred zero times at v1. suppliedBy is per-class across all four items — three NT-8, one NT-7 — so the mapping that made the hole invisible is on the page, and EV-2's unbacked clause is replaced by a routing statement. B2 landed cleanly: both classes now have objects whose name, input and pass are character-exact against preview-analyze-contract.v2's negativeTests, each with its own intent, pass and source, and NT-8's suppliesMembers lists the three live members exactly. SF1 landed within the new constraint: d9-exit-contract.v1.14 is pinned by path and digest, membership points at that pin in two places, and I tested rather than trusted the non-enumeration — a D9-code-shaped token regex over the whole artifact returns none. Nothing regressed; zero paths removed. What is left is a labelling defect inside the B1 repair. The live evidence cell has three members and the subject quotes it correctly, but retainedEvidence now holds four entries, and the fourth is labelled memberVerbatim while carrying 'host must not mint fail/warn other than core policyOutcome' — which is not a live member. It is the claim's first limb with the leading capital dropped, so it is a near-verbatim claim quote rather than an invention; but the field name asserts membership it does not have, NT-7's suppliesMembers gives a third wording that quotes nothing, and no sentence anywhere records that the live cell has three members while four are retained. Every sibling keys retainedEvidence to the live cell and carries a block enumerating those members. The harm is bounded, since liveCellVerbatim sits in the same file, which is why this is a SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker. I want it on the record that I partly invited this: my v1 repair note offered a fourth retained item bound to the claim's first limb as an acceptable shape and said nothing about how to label it. The repair is a few words — quote the limb exactly, put it under a field that says it is a claim limb rather than a member, make NT-7's supplies list use the same string, and add one sentence recording the three-versus-four. Two advisories carry, one partly addressed: failsIf now exists with three self-tests where v1 had none, but the assurance-stage and status cells are still dropped and there is still no whatThisCloses or OBL- identifier for a recorder to attach to; and namedExecutesLimbs still carries bare NT ids against the live DR-131/DR-133 NT-7 collision, now resolvable in two places rather than one.
